target_review.notes: The frozen target accurately records the approved nontrivial interpretation (locally uniform spatial constancy at q), all three hypotheses, positive n,m, interior-time scope, Hilbert–Schmidt gradient, and the required actual integrability plus differentiability/conservation—not a totalized integral. The candidate proposition P matches the stated conclusion. However closure is not established: N003 relies on unsubstantiated analysis/source applicability, so the candidate does not prove the complete target. Edge conditions include no claim at t=0 and no regularity of the scalar multiplier.

D001.notes: Energy density is explicitly a scalar sum of squared Euclidean norms, identifies the Frobenius/Hilbert–Schmidt convention, and binds x,r with the stated domains. No theorem is built into the definition.

D002.notes: E is declared positive-reals→R by the definition, but an unrestricted Lebesgue integral of a nonnegative measurable density need not be finite and naturally has extended-real value. The target explicitly requires proving integrability before conservation and rejects a totalized nonintegrable integral. Defining E as real-valued integral without a finiteness prerequisite/extended-real codomain is not a complete coherent definition for all allowed inputs; it cannot itself supply finiteness.

D003.notes: The Laplacian is defined as the componentwise finite sum of second spatial derivatives on the stated smooth map; it adds no PDE conclusion.

D004.notes: The intended Euclidean/Borel/Lebesgue structure is described, but the statement identifies product one-dimensional Lebesgue volume with Lebesgue measure on R^k without a precise construction/normalization argument. This measure setup is used in source applicability and is not itself an imported theorem.

M001.notes: The supplied full telescope includes measurable/topological structures, normed additive group, measurable opens, and finite-on-compacts; the continuous and compact-support arguments are explicit. Source definition is a theorem, not a definition. Application requires the stated Euclidean volume instance.

M005.notes: Full signature has two topological-space instances and compactness of both factors; the prose product statement is faithful up to product notation. No hidden assumptions beyond these.

M006.notes: Full signature/probe records required measurability, scalar and normed-space instances and all hypotheses. But the candidate's actual use must establish local a.e. strong measurability, integrability at the base time, derivative measurability, an integrable dominating function, and pointwise-in-parameter derivative on an open neighborhood. The candidate's N001/N002 formulations do not exhibit a proved integrable dominating bound from compact support and uniform-in-time support; N002's stated conclusion does not include a domination bound. The theorem therefore cannot establish the asserted derivative merely from its listed contract. Official source read confirms this is a dominated differentiation theorem, not an unconditional differentiability result.

M009.notes: Complete signature and restatement include integrability on s and measurability of s; output is integrability of the indicator. This is not a general extension-by-zero theorem without those premises.

M011.notes: The complete signature requires three integrability premises, differentiability on the topological supports of the opposite factors, and a real bilinear continuous map/Haar setting. The candidate's asserted spatial integration by parts must demonstrate these premises and the precise bilinear pairing/application; the recorded source statement is not evidence that the actual compactly-supported vector fields satisfy all those obligations. No adequate completed application review is present in the material inspected. Official source is an integration-by-parts theorem, not a bare identity.

Compact support alone controls support, not uniform magnitude of the time derivative on the common compact set absent a proved compactness/continuity boundedness argument.
